newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn Fin Min not ready to cut tax revenue estimate.
newsitem.headline: Bonn Fin Min not ready to cut tax revenue estimate.

text.p: The German Finance Ministry said on Wednesday it still saw no reason to lower estimates for 1997 tax revenue.

There was no concrete indication for correcting the forecast of a work group on tax revenues, a spokeswoman told Reuters. The group revised its forecast in May, saying 1997 tax reveune would be 18 billion marks ($9.6 billion) below the previous official estimate.
Bonn Fin Min not ready to cut tax revenue estimate
"According to available information, we are on track," the finance ministry spokeswoman said.

The Bundesbank in a recent monthly report said tax revenue would fall below the May estimate. A sluggish economy and record unemployment have caused tax revenues to decline, endangering Germany's effort to qualify for European economic and monetary union (EMU).
The ministry spokesman said Germany would fulfill the EMU goal for total public budget deficits of not more than three percent of gross domestic product.
